description: SKELETON — NOT A REAL EXPORT. This file lists the charts the Story factory dashboard carries (REPO-DESIGN.md §9.4) so reviewers can see what the §15.6 maintainer release builds; it is not an export and its keys are NOT the export's keys, which are not guessed. The release builds the dashboard once by hand over the three Record types in a maintainer dev team, exports it, and saves the export here, replacing this file entirely; ./scripts/kit bundle then carries it to [KIT] 00 A23 (POST /api/v1/dashboards/import {team_id, data, mode: new, new_name: Story factory}). Until then A23's import is expected to fail and the setup report says so. The release check (kit.yml job release; ./scripts/sdlc check --release, release_not_skeleton) fails while this description starts with SKELETON. Import resolves record charts against existing types by record_type_name: VERIFY K17. Dashboards chart Records and Cases only; record charts live only on team dashboards (the ops team); JSON fields are not filterable and are never used; the charts count and filter on TEXT_ENUM, NUMBER and TIMESTAMP fields, and two group by a TEXT field (owner, story_key), which the §15.6 release confirms.
name: Story factory
skeleton_scope: team dashboard in the ops team (the manifest's prod team)

skeleton_limits.snapshots: email on a schedule: 10 per dashboard, 50 recipients each

skeleton_intended_charts.title: Phase by owner
skeleton_intended_charts.note: owner is a TEXT field; whether a stacked chart can group by TEXT is part of what the release confirms

skeleton_intended_charts.title: Specialist runs and credits over time
skeleton_intended_charts.group_by: created_at period: week if the chart can group by time, else day (the export decides)

skeleton_intended_notes.title: Gates and who decides
skeleton_intended_notes.markdown: G0 intake triage (owner or a G0 approver; the gate_decision Page) · G1 readiness (./scripts/sdlc ready) · G2 design approval (a CODEOWNER merges the design PR) · G3 plan approval (/sdlc-gate) · G4 verify and merge (CI + CODEOWNER + a human merge) · G5a first ship (the GitHub production environment's reviewer) · G5b change request (a named approver in Tines) · G6 go-live and G7 ownership review (the gate_decision Page) · GB budget (opened by code, released by a human) · GX escalation (the owner). The rules: sdlc/gates/README.md in the repository.
